newsitem.title: USA: 3M profits cut by currency, sees solid '97.
newsitem.headline: 3M profits cut by currency, sees solid '97.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co said Tuesday that changes in currency exchange rates cut fourth-quarter profits by about five percent, or $0.04 per share.
Before the effects of currency exchange rates, earnings from continuing operations were $0.90 per share, up from $0.63 in the year-ago quarter.
The diversified manufacturer said it expects "solid sales and earnings growth again in 1997."
"Our technology base and new product portfolio are the strongest in our history," said 3M Chairman and Chief Executive L.D. DeSimone.
Fourth-quarter sales totaled $3.62 billion, up 9.6 percent from a year earlier. Without changes in currency exchange rates, sales rose about 12 percent, 3M said.

For the year, earnings per share from continuing operations rose 12.4 percent to $3.63. Income from continuing operations totaled $1.52 billion, up 11.7 percent from 1995. Currency effects reduced 1996 earnings by about $0.15 per share, or about five percent.
